questions.prompt: What path does a charged particle follow if it enters a uniform magnetic field with velocity perpendicular to the field?
questions.answer: It follows a circular path, assuming no other forces act. The magnetic force supplies the centripetal force.

questions.prompt: State the radius of circular motion for a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field.
questions.answer:
The radius is
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}
\]
for speed perpendicular to the field.

questions.prompt: What happens to the speed of a charged particle moving in a magnetic field if no other forces act?
questions.answer: The speed remains constant because magnetic force does no work.

questions.prompt: Derive the circular-path radius from magnetic force and centripetal force.
questions.answer:
Set magnetic force equal to radial force:
\[
|q|vB=m\frac{v^2}{r}
\]
Cancel one factor of \(v\):
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}
\]

questions.prompt: A proton moves at \(2.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) perpendicular to \(0.50\,\mathrm{T}\). Find its circular radius.
An electron moves at \(3.0\times10^6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) perpendicular to \(0.020\,\mathrm{T}\). Find its circular radius.
How does the radius change if the particle speed doubles while \(m\), \(|q|\), and \(B\) stay fixed?
questions.answer:
Since
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}
\]
the radius is directly proportional to speed. Doubling \(v\) doubles \(r\).

questions.prompt: How does the radius change if the magnetic field doubles while \(m\), \(|q|\), and \(v\) stay fixed?
questions.answer:
Since
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}
\]
the radius is inversely proportional to \(B\). Doubling \(B\) halves \(r\).

questions.prompt: State the angular speed of circular motion for a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field.
questions.answer:
The angular speed is
\[
\omega=\frac{|q|B}{m}
\]

questions.prompt: State the period of circular motion for a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field.
questions.answer:
The period is
\[
T=\frac{2\pi m}{|q|B}
\]
for nonrelativistic motion in a uniform magnetic field.

questions.prompt: A particle has velocity with components both perpendicular and parallel to \(\vec B\). What kind of path results?
questions.answer: The perpendicular component produces circular motion, while the parallel component remains unchanged. The combined path is a helix.

questions.prompt: In helical motion, which speed component determines the radius?
questions.answer:
The perpendicular component determines the radius:
\[
r=\frac{mv_\perp}{|q|B}
\]

questions.prompt: What happens to the curvature direction if the sign of the charge is reversed?
questions.answer: The curvature direction reverses because the magnetic force direction depends on the sign of \(q\). The radius magnitude is unchanged if \(|q|\), \(m\), \(v\), and \(B\) are unchanged.

questions.prompt: A singly charged ion moves in a circle of radius \(0.20\,\mathrm{m}\) at speed \(4.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in \(0.30\,\mathrm{T}\). Find its mass.
A charged particle has momentum \(p\) perpendicular to a magnetic field. Express its orbit radius in terms of \(p\).
questions.answer:
Since \(p=mv\),
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}=\frac{p}{|q|B}
\]

questions.prompt: Find the magnetic field needed for a proton moving at \(1.0\times10^6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to have radius \(0.10\,\mathrm{m}\).
Why does the period not depend on speed for nonrelativistic circular motion in a uniform magnetic field?
questions.answer:
The radius grows in proportion to speed:
\[
r=\frac{mv}{|q|B}
\]
The period is circumference over speed:
\[
T=\frac{2\pi r}{v}=\frac{2\pi m}{|q|B}
\]
The speed cancels.

questions.prompt: A particle enters a magnetic field with kinetic energy doubled. How does the circular radius change if \(B\), \(m\), and \(|q|\) stay fixed?
questions.answer: For fixed mass, \(K=\tfrac12mv^2\), so doubling \(K\) increases speed by \(\sqrt2\). Since \(r\propto v\), the radius increases by \(\sqrt2\).

questions.prompt: A helical path has parallel speed \(v_\parallel\) and period \(T\). What is the pitch of the helix?
questions.answer:
The pitch is the distance advanced parallel to the field in one period:
\[
\text{pitch}=v_\parallel T= v_\parallel\frac{2\pi m}{|q|B}
\]

questions.prompt: Derive the helical motion model for a charged particle entering a uniform magnetic field at an arbitrary angle.
questions.answer:
Split velocity into components:
\[
\vec v=\vec v_\perp+\vec v_\parallel
\]
The parallel component gives no magnetic force, so it remains constant. The perpendicular component feels \(|q|v_\perp B\), which supplies centripetal force:
\[
r=\frac{mv_\perp}{|q|B}
\]
Combining uniform motion along \(\vec B\) with circular motion perpendicular to \(\vec B\) gives a helix.
